gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, SM89
ratio_definition: raw bytes / compressed bytes; >1 means storage saved
findings: Dense final GPU uint32 NTT: whole-buffer Zstd1/3/9 ratio about 1.000, LZ4 about 0.996. No useful byte-codec compression in this corpus.
Dense CPU uint64 NTT: Zstd3 about 2.1x, LZ4 about 1.34x. GPU already uses uint32; CPU storage gains must not be reported as GPU gains.
Dense normalized FP64 FFT: Zstd3 about 1.04x, LZ4 slightly expands.

Dense rounded integer coefficients require 30 zigzag bits in all formal runs. Exact real antisymmetry permits half storage: 122888 bytes per plaintext at batch1, about 120KiB. GPU reduction about 17.07x at Q8 and 68.26x at Q32.
Half coefficients are lossless relative to CPU Encode; they are tied to scale. Real symmetry is checked before enabling. Complex inputs and >63-bit codes require another format.

A verified periodic1024 slot corpus has 32-fold exact NTT replication groups in Poseidon bit-reversed order. Direct group storage is 64KiB/Q8 or 256KiB/Q32; upload+CUDA replication takes 25.4us or 67.5us per plaintext at batch1.

Traditional byte codecs compress that periodic GPU NTT by about 33x/Zstd3 and 16x/LZ4. Periodic half coefficients plus Zstd3 reach about 5KiB, but they require entropy decode, RNS and NTT; not a claim for dense Qwen weights.

Dense half coefficients: H2D+CUDA RNS+CUDA NTT takes about 56.1us/Q8 and 163.8us/Q32 at batch1; H2D+CUDA RNS+TileLang Tensor NTT takes 107.8us/Q8 and 368.6us/Q32. Tensor NTT has 12 Tensor stages and 4 CUDA stages; unpack and modular work use CUDA.

On dense GPU NTT, nvCOMP LZ4 device decode about 273us/pt at batch1; Zstd about 3.53ms/Q8 and 3.69ms/Q32. Batch8 increases output throughput; see summary. nsight confirms most elapsed work is in GPU decompress kernels.

Prefer fixed-width half integer coefficients for dense real weights in this parameter range; verified repeated NTT can use replication or a future compressed-aware multiply_plain. Fusing unpack/RNS into the first Tensor NTT stage is a future optimization, not implemented.
limitations: Synthetic Gaussian/prefix/periodic/scalar corpora, not pretrained Qwen. Compression ratios vary with scale, magnitude, packing and modulus count.
No full Qwen/CKKS end-to-end run or concurrent foreground interference measurement in this study.
CPU preprocessing/compression, allocations, tables and codec configuration excluded from GPU runtime timings. GPU output still needs a full materialized NTT buffer.
C++ event timing includes host submission gaps; nvCOMP Python API event timing includes Python/dispatch gaps. Nsight diagnostics separately measure device kernels.
nvCOMP native64KiB chunks encoded on GPU during setup. CPU-produced compressed payload interoperability was not tested; batch8 tiles the same payload.
Repeated CUDA Graph replay failed with SIGSEGV for the current nvCOMP/PyTorch dependency combination; not used in formal results, experimental graph option removed. Root cause not established.
188Server SOCKSv5 Host unreachable; local GPU only. Clocks not locked.
Only optional benchmark code/build target changed; no production kernel, compiler IR or runtime integration in this study.

sources.title: WPC: Weight Plaintext Compression for CNN Inference based on RNS-CKKS, CCS 2025
sources.findings: Periodicity can be preserved through CKKS slot encoding and negacyclic NTT. Their CNN-specific packing reports 46.08-139.11x whole-model weight-plaintext compression and 1.25-2.18x speedup on A100. It does not establish those ratios for Qwen/Transformers. Different NTT orderings need different replication indexing.

sources.title: ZipServ: Fast and Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Hardware-Aware Lossless Compression, ASPLOS 2026
sources.findings: Lossless BF16 weight compression of up to 30% size reduction. ALU units decode weights while Tensor Cores perform the following GEMM. Supports fusing unpack with the consuming matrix operation, not calling LZ4/Zstd bitstream decode Tensor Core arithmetic.

sources.title: NVIDIA nvCOMP Algorithm Selection
sources.findings: nvCOMP provides CUDA LZ4/Zstd and other codecs. Algorithm choice is data dependent. Hardware DE is distinct from Tensor Cores.

sources.title: NVIDIA nvCOMP Decompression Engine FAQ
sources.findings: Dedicated DE on supported B200/B300/GB200/GB300 GPUs, advertised up to 600GB/s. Supports LZ4/Snappy/Deflate/Gzip; not present on the local Ada RTX4060. This is not a measured result for our hardware.
